--- title: Download data with Python execute: eval: true --- ### Set up required libraries ::: {#e88acf22 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd import os import rasterio from matplotlib import pyplot as plt from PIL import Image import numpy as np import tarfile import pyprojroot import requests import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET ``` ::: ### Set up work and output directories We use library `pyprojroot` to define relative paths from our repository root folder: ::: {#20cec2d2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} repodir = pyprojroot.find_root(pyprojroot.has_dir(".git")) ``` ::: ## Profile information from OSF Workbook with profile content for Ecosystem Functional Groups of the IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology (Level 3 units) available at We can read this workbook directly from the url using `pandas`: ::: {#35133d5f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} profiles_url='https://osf.io/download/4dcea/' EFG_profiles = pd.read_excel(profiles_url, sheet_name = 'Short description') ``` ::: Here is a peak of the downloaded file: ::: {#6c0fd889 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} EFG_profiles[['name','short description', 'url']].head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Indicative map data download from zenodo Indicative maps are available from different Zenodo repositories. ### Bundle of indicative maps One repository holds the bundle of maps in compressed tar archives. This record id automatically resolves to the latest version: ::: {#3b8caded .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} record_url = 'https://zenodo.org/api/records/3546513' r = requests.get(record_url) ``` ::: Check the difference between the `id` and `conceptid`, and the two DOI (digital object identifier): ::: {#20f58baa .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} response = r.json() print((response['id'], response['conceptrecid'], response['doi'], response['conceptdoi'])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` (10081251, '3546513', '10.5281/zenodo.10081251', '10.5281/zenodo.3546513') ``` ::: ::: We will create a folder for this direct download from zenodo for the latest version of the bundle: ::: {#5cb31c0f .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} datadir = repodir / "gisdata" / "indicative-maps-bundle" / "latest" datadir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) ``` ::: The zenodo record has four different files: ::: {#ee998e41 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} response['files'] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ``` [{'id': 'fe0bbd7a-bc60-415f-a8f6-6848acd8c220', 'key': 'README.md', 'size': 19383, 'checksum': 'md5:e6cdcb4b46b261fecd5fce5c31fb5805', 'links': {'self': 'https://zenodo.org/api/records/10081251/files/README.md/content'}}, {'id': '437d31b3-6502-454a-9511-da1432b22d1f', 'key': 'all-maps-vector-geojson.tar.bz2', 'size': 853479699, 'checksum': 'md5:8490adfd971bc3a5b02cc72832e2df3e', 'links': {'self': 'https://zenodo.org/api/records/10081251/files/all-maps-vector-geojson.tar.bz2/content'}}, {'id': 'd2cb3226-e68c-452d-a6f8-a65d0686380b', 'key': 'all-maps-raster-geotiff.tar.bz2', 'size': 157378816, 'checksum': 'md5:245d09d535609d1c010eff52e9c8bfaa', 'links': {'self': 'https://zenodo.org/api/records/10081251/files/all-maps-raster-geotiff.tar.bz2/content'}}, {'id': 'a42361fc-e4bc-48d3-8c8a-0deafa722f80', 'key': 'map-details.xml', 'size': 114612, 'checksum': 'md5:5177a7a6fc5aa4981088093a68b2964e', 'links': {'self': 'https://zenodo.org/api/records/10081251/files/map-details.xml/content'}}] ``` ::: ::: We want to download three of them: ::: {#970064c4 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} for i in range(len(response['files'])): zenodo_url = response['files'][i]['links']['self'] outputfile = datadir / response['files'][i]['key'] if not outputfile.exists(): zdownload = requests.get(zenodo_url) if zdownload.ok: with open(outputfile, mode="wb") as file: file.write(zdownload.content) ``` ::: We extract maps from the tar archives in a sandbox folder: ::: {#69e3805f .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} sandbox = repodir / "sandbox" / "latest" sandbox.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) ``` ::: ::: {#c492acb4 .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} maps_tar = datadir / 'all-maps-raster-geotiff.tar.bz2' with tarfile.open(maps_tar) as my_tarfile: if hasattr(tarfile, 'data_filter'): my_tarfile.extractall(path=sandbox,filter='data') else: # remove this when no longer needed, see https://docs.python.org/3/library/tarfile.html#tarfile-extraction-filter print('Extracting may be unsafe; consider updating Python') my_tarfile.extractall(path=sandbox) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Extracting may be unsafe; consider updating Python ``` ::: ::: ### Repositories for single EFG maps Map details are stored in a xml file that is part of the map bundle zenodo download. Check the file was downloaded: ::: {#ba254f45 .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} map_details_file = datadir / "map-details.xml" map_details_file.exists() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=12} ``` True ``` ::: ::: We'll use the `xml2` library to read the xml file ::: {#9f38c163 .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} tree = ET.parse(map_details_file) #maplist_root = tree.getroot() ``` ::: We can query map details for an specific map: ::: {#9e915b5b .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} node=tree.find(".//Map[@efg_code='T1.1']") for child in node.iter(): print(ET.tostring(child)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` b'\n T1.1 Tropical/Subtropical lowland rainforests\n Major and minor occurrences were initially identified using consensus land-cover maps (Tuanmu et al. 2014) and then cropped to selected terrestrial ecoregions (Dinerstein et al. 2017; DAWE 2012) at 30 arc seconds spatial resolution. Ecoregions were selected if: i) their descriptions mentioned features consistent with those identified in the profile of the Ecosystem Functional Group; and ii) if their location was consistent with the ecological drivers described in the profile.\n \n JR Ferrer-Paris\n DA Keith\n \n 10.5281/zenodo.5090450\n \n ' b'T1.1 Tropical/Subtropical lowland rainforests\n ' b'Major and minor occurrences were initially identified using consensus land-cover maps (Tuanmu et al. 2014) and then cropped to selected terrestrial ecoregions (Dinerstein et al. 2017; DAWE 2012) at 30 arc seconds spatial resolution. Ecoregions were selected if: i) their descriptions mentioned features consistent with those identified in the profile of the Ecosystem Functional Group; and ii) if their location was consistent with the ecological drivers described in the profile.\n ' b'\n JR Ferrer-Paris\n DA Keith\n \n ' b'JR Ferrer-Paris\n ' b'DA Keith\n ' b'10.5281/zenodo.5090450\n ' ``` ::: ::: The field with doi for the individual map are stored in the `Dataset-doi` tag. We can run a query for all elements containing this tag and summarise this using list comprehension: ::: {#d8c8dd75 .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} all_dois = [doi.text for doi in tree.findall( ".//Dataset-doi")] ``` ::: Now we use this list of DOIs to download a copy of each of the repositories containing files for each ecosystem functional group: ::: {#cc6f7e94 .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} for doi in all_dois: out_folder = repodir / "gisdata" / "indicative-maps" / doi out_folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) if len(os.listdir(out_folder)) ==0: # query doi to get the corresponding zenodo API url r = requests.get('https://doi.org/'+doi, allow_redirects=True) parsed_uri = urlparse(r.url) zenodo_url = '{uri.scheme}://{uri.netloc}/api{uri.path}'.format(uri=parsed_uri) r.close() # now query the API r = requests.get(zenodo_url) response = r.json() for i in range(len(response['files'])): zenodo_url = response['files'][i]['links']['self'] outputfile = out_folder / response['files'][i]['key'] if not outputfile.exists(): zdownload = requests.get(zenodo_url) if zdownload.ok: with open(outputfile, mode="wb") as file: file.write(zdownload.content) ``` ::: ### Compare downloaded files Now we have two copies of each map file, one in the sandbox folder (extracted from the map bundle), and one downloaded directly from the corresponding record. Map code and version are described in the map attributes in the xml file: ::: {#d6a0d255 .cell execution_count=17} ``` {.python .cell-code} node=tree.find(".//Map[@efg_code='T1.3']") node.attrib ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=17} ``` {'efg_code': 'T1.3', 'map_code': 'T1.3.WM.nwx', 'map_version': 'v1.0', 'update': '2021-11-26'} ``` ::: ::: The file extracted from the tar archive uses the same code and version combination for the file name: ::: {#552fac20 .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} for k in sandbox.glob("%s*.tif" % node.attrib['efg_code']): print(k.name) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` T1.3.WM.nwx_v1.0.tif ``` ::: ::: As well as the file downloaded from the specific repository: ::: {#b44c3408 .cell execution_count=19} ``` {.python .cell-code} out_folder = repodir / "gisdata" / "indicative-maps" / node.find('Dataset-doi').text for k in out_folder.glob("%s*.tif" % node.attrib['efg_code']): print(k.name) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` T1.3.WM.nwx_v1.0.tif ``` ::: ::: #### Raster maps We'll use the `rasterio` to read and plot the raster file ::: {#a7fab4ca .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} src = rasterio.open(k) plt.imshow(src.read(1), cmap='pink') plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](download-with-python_files/figure-html/cell-21-output-1.png){width=612 height=307} ::: ::: Compare this with the thumbnail downloaded from Zenodo: ::: {#ca4423c8 .cell execution_count=21} ``` {.python .cell-code} pngfile = [x for x in out_folder.glob("*.png")] img = np.asarray(Image.open(pngfile[0])) plt.imshow(img) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](download-with-python_files/figure-html/cell-22-output-1.png){width=583 height=372} ::: :::
